papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.abstract: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: The index from a super-point
papers.abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The associated VOA for the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory is given by the Feigin--Feigin--Tipunin $\mathcal{A}(6)$ algebra. The arc space of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of $\mathcal{A}(6)$ does not reproduce the vacuum character, and therefore $\mathcal{A}(6)$ is not classically free. Supplementing Zhu's $C_2$-algebra by three relations in the first jet ring, the generalized arc space reproduces the Macdonald index of $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ up to, at least, order $q^{51}$.

papers.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
papers.abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.abstract: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

papers.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
papers.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.

papers.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

papers.title: Frobenius $2$-algebras and $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix. Thus, our construction provides a categorical generalization of Kashaev's construction.

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $\phi_1(p,q)$ and $\phi_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $\phi_1-$fermionic, $\phi_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.

papers.title: An all-orders proof of gradient flow for multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof uses the Weyl consistency conditions of Osborn and Jack, and it assumes two properties of perturbation theory: that the generating functional with local couplings is finite (also assumed by Osborn and Jack), and that the known expansion of massive Feynman integrals at large momenta holds with a bound on its remainder at each momentum. The consistency conditions give a gradient formula in which the tensor that multiplies the beta function is allowed to have an antisymmetric part, determined by coefficients of the Weyl anomaly. We derive a Ward identity for the two-point function of the marginal operators at constant couplings away from fixed points, with sources for the currents of field rotations and for the mass operator. It re-expresses one of the anti-symmetric contributions in terms of two-point functions and the first moment of the three-point function. We show that, after this rewrite, each of the resulting terms is equivalent to a symmetric contribution to the metric and a contribution to the potential, and we give both explicitly. The metric is positive definite to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof implies in particular the four relations among five- and six-loop coefficients of the field rotation, which Pannell and Stergiou derived as the conditions for a gradient flow at six loops. We check by explicit computation that these relations indeed hold. A companion paper treats $d=4-\varepsilon$ and other critical dimensions with a Ward identity on the sphere.

papers.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.

papers.title: M\"obius Fusion Algebra
papers.abstract: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the M\"obius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the M\"obius band, where the orientation-reversal of the M\"obius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula, in the context of Reshetikhin-Turaev-type topological quantum field theories on non-orientable manifolds.

papers.title: Infrared finite scattering theory: Non-relativistic Coulomb scattering
papers.abstract: We revisit non-relativistic quantum-mechanical scattering in a Coulomb potential. The long-range nature of the interaction leads to divergent integrals in conventional S-matrix calculations using the Born series. Dollard showed that a well-defined scattering operator can be constructed by replacing the free Hamiltonian $ H_0 $ with an appropriate asymptotic Hamiltonian $ H_{\rm D} $. However, explicit perturbative calculations within Dollard's framework have remained scarce. We develop a perturbative formulation of the Dollard scattering operator in which the Coulomb divergences cancel to all orders. Perturbatively, we demonstrate this cancellation explicitly through second Born order and show that the resulting amplitude reproduces the known exact distributional Coulomb amplitude, including its forward-scattering contribution. With the aim of generalizing our analysis to quantum field theory, we reformulate the problem in the Heisenberg picture. We construct a new set of canonical variables through a time-dependent canonical transformation that removes the logarithmic Coulomb correction from the asymptotic phase-space coordinates. Using these variables, we construct the corresponding Heisenberg S-matrix through several complementary approaches. This leads to a formulation of the Lehmann--Symanzik--Zimmermann (LSZ) reduction formalism adapted to the modified asymptotic dynamics, which we relate to the Dollard scattering operator. This construction provides a framework for extending the LSZ formalism to infrared divergences in relativistic quantum field theories with long-range interactions and massless fields.

papers.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
papers.abstract: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $\tau$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $\tau$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.

papers.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.

papers.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
papers.abstract: We perform the complete light-cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $\kappa$-symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which in its turn is required to be nonvanaishing and nontrivial in this limit. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.

papers.title: Localisation with on-shell supersymmetry algebras via the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism: Localisation as gauge fixing
papers.abstract: The Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism provides a powerful technique to deal with gauge and global (super)symmetries that may only hold on shell. We argue that, since global (super)symmetries and gauge symmetries appear on an equal footing in the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, similarly localisation with respect to global (super)symmetries appears on an equal footing with gauge fixing of gauge symmetries; in general, when the gauge-fixing condition is not invariant under the global symmetries, localisation (with respect to a localising fermion) and gauge fixing (with respect to a gauge-fixing fermion) combine into a single operation. Furthermore, this perspective enables supersymmetric localisation using only on-shell supermultiplets, dispensing with auxiliary fields, extending an insight first discovered by Losev and Lysov arXiv:2312.13999. We provide the first examples of on-shell localisation for quantum field theories (together with a companion paper by Arvanitakis arXiv:2511.00144).

papers.title: Integrability from Homotopy Algebras
papers.abstract: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in the study of field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. The semi-classical equivalence of the two theories is expected on general grounds, as the principal chiral model arises by eliminating trivial pairs and gauge fixing. We construct this equivalence explicitly as an off-shell, cyclic quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing the two theories, and show that it directly encodes the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.

papers.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
papers.abstract: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.

papers.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
papers.abstract: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

papers.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.abstract: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

papers.title: A hyperbolicity obstruction near regular charged centers
papers.abstract: A conserved charge creates a tension at a spherical center: the flux remains fixed while the area of the symmetry spheres shrinks. We ask whether curvature-dependent electromagnetic responses can reconcile bounded central curvature with hyperbolic propagation in four-dimensional Einstein gravity when both parity-even and parity-odd couplings are allowed. The background equations force a positive charge potential and its first curvature derivative to vanish at the central curvature endpoint. On branches with a positive electromagnetic kinetic coefficient and a positive effective gravitational coefficient, this endpoint flattening produces a physical extraordinary mode of the fully coupled equations whose squared angular characteristic speed is strictly below minus one at radii arbitrarily close to the center. Its characteristic cone has no hyperbolicity direction in common with the ordinary photon and graviton modes. The result requires no central curvature expansion, remains valid at points where the curvature Legendre Hessian vanishes, and extends to positive-definite mixing of finitely many Abelian fields. An exact analytic example with a nonlinear gravitational curvature sector admits a real, subluminal extraordinary photon cone near the center. In a fixed-action black-hole family, the obstruction extends outside the outer horizon over a near-extremal parameter interval.

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.abstract: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.

papers.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
papers.abstract: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},\chi_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1\sigma$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $\Lambda$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

papers.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

papers.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.
